option.counterfactual: Every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of S² × S² with finitely many fixed points has at least four fixed points, even when they are degenerate.
option.approach: Check precise versions of the degenerate Arnold theorem applicable to S² × S², then combine any four-point lower bound with independent rotations of the two spheres to establish sharpness.

judge.reason: It claims the minimum is 4, exactly the same value claimed by e2.

options.counterfactual: There is no four-fixed-point lower bound for degenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of the equal-area product S² × S²; the minimum is three.
options.approach: Investigate an explicitly time-dependent Hamiltonian with three fixed points. A construction would need two ordinary fixed points and a degenerate fixed point of local index two, consistent with the Lefschetz number four.

options.counterfactual: There is no four-fixed-point lower bound for degenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of the equal-area product S² × S²; the minimum is three.
options.approach: Examine smooth functions on S² × S² with exactly three critical points without assuming that the two middle critical points of the height-sum function can be merged. Such a function would give the desired Hamiltonian after sufficiently small scaling.

options.counterfactual: There is no four-fixed-point lower bound for degenerate Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of the equal-area product S² × S²; the minimum is three.
options.approach: Check whether a generating-function construction can produce three fixed points even if no autonomous Hamiltonian can. Generating functions may involve auxiliary variables and therefore need not have the same critical-point restrictions as functions on S² × S² itself.

options.counterfactual: A theorem about the minimum number of critical points of smooth functions on S² × S² does not determine the minimum number of fixed points of time-dependent Hamiltonian maps.
options.approach: Analyze genuinely time-dependent compositions of Hamiltonian flows rather than restricting to small autonomous Hamiltonians. Their fixed-point equations may admit configurations that cannot arise as the critical points of a function on the manifold.

options.counterfactual: A theorem about the minimum number of critical points of smooth functions on S² × S² does not determine the minimum number of fixed points of time-dependent Hamiltonian maps.
options.approach: Identify exactly which version of the Arnold conjecture compares Hamiltonian fixed points with critical points, and whether that version has been proved for this manifold with degeneracy allowed. This would establish whether critical-point topology can legitimately supply the lower bound.

options.counterfactual: A theorem about the minimum number of critical points of smooth functions on S² × S² does not determine the minimum number of fixed points of time-dependent Hamiltonian maps.
options.approach: Study the graph of the Hamiltonian map intersecting the diagonal in the product symplectic manifold. This reformulates the problem as a Lagrangian intersection count without assuming that the intersections come from a function on S² × S².
